title: Meat Lover's Carnivore Board
seo_title: Meat Lover's Charcuterie Board for 8–12: Six Cured Meats
description: A meat lover's charcuterie board for 8–12: prosciutto, soppressata, bresaola, speck, pepperoni and coppa with aged Parmesan, mustard, cornichons and olives.
hook: Six cured meats, one cheese and maximum flavor: the board for people who skip straight to the salami.
why: Six meats, tasted from mild to intense, and each one shown the way its texture needs: prosciutto in loose folds, soppressata and pepperoni folded or fanned, bresaola lying flat, speck and coppa in ribbons. Get the display wrong and good meat eats badly.
One aged Parmesan is all the cheese it needs. Mustard, cornichons and olives cut the fat, and fig jam and apricots add sweetness against the salt.

timeline.what: Take the Parmesan out of the fridge.
Take out the meats; fill the condiment bowls.
Place the meats from mild to strong.
Add the Parmesan, olives, fruit and crackers.

faq.q: What meats go on a charcuterie board?
faq.a: A mix of whole-muscle cuts (prosciutto, speck, coppa, bresaola) and salami (soppressata, pepperoni) gives the best range of textures and flavors.
About 2 to 3 oz per person, or more when it's the main food. With six meats, about ½ oz of each per guest.

faq.q: What cheese goes with a meat-heavy board?
faq.a: One hard, salty cheese like aged Parmesan or Pecorino. It stands up to the meats without competing.
